Codes are local program competencies, not official benchmarks. Each individual lesson claims only what students actually practice and demonstrate. Not every unit needs every domain. Arts must include purposeful choices and communication; counting decoration as art or a tablet as computing is insufficient.

docs.title: Grade-specific progression and memorable experiences
docs.text:
Grade Entry/prerequisite to establish End-of-grade performance to seek Signature experience and next step K Follow one modeled oral instruction; compare visible objects Observe, build, point/draw/tell one change; count/compare a small set Structures that connect/help; next explain a problem and simple instruction sequence 1 Reestablish safe tool use, oral sequencing and counting Build for a purpose, trace a short sequence, describe a result Paper bridge; next explain choices and represent results 2 Repeat Grade 1 demonstrations rather than assume they were taught in the other rotation Explain design choice, compare measured results and revise an algorithm/design A service structure/mechanism with a before/after explanation; next conduct fair tests 3 Model criteria, test procedure, measurement units and a simple table Test a design under fixed conditions and use evidence to suggest a revision Measured bridge; next use repeated measures and clearer evidence 4 Recheck fair testing, recording and distinguishing prediction from result Use measurements and evidence to improve a design or explanation Structures, indoor weather inquiry or safe circuits; next compare against multiple criteria 5 Establish criteria/constraints, repeated observations and respectful feedback Compare designs using evidence, criteria, cost/resources and an ethical reason Service design or environmental model; next defend a tradeoff and identify limitations 6 Reestablish data quality, computational trace and explanation of users' needs Defend design choices with evidence, tradeoffs, cost, ethics and performance Inclusive design exhibition or fictional evidence investigation; next transfer methods to independent inquiry

These are desired local outcomes, not automatic promotions based on exposure. The learning progression gives competency-level introduced/developing/reinforced/expected indicators and individual evidence.

docs.title: Rotations and prerequisites
docs.text:
Year A and B are alternative entry years, not beginner/advanced levels. Every rotation must reintroduce the design cycle, safe tool routines, relevant vocabulary, measurement method and computing representations. Younger students receive modeling and accessible responses; older students extend evidence, independence and justification.

Repeat the skill intentionally, not an identical worksheet or unexamined product. Keep a small portfolio so a returning student can compare earlier and later reasoning. When a project recurs, increase only an appropriate dimension: independence, precision, data, number of criteria or ethical tradeoffs.

docs.title: Seasonal and workload controls
docs.text:
• No required objective depends on outdoor access in a Minnesota winter. Use room-temperature materials, safe indoor observations and prepared data when appropriate; do not claim a paper model supplies real weather data.
  • Growing investigations require observations over time. Schedule follow-up checks explicitly; a single period cannot demonstrate a life cycle.
  • Start with reusable kits and common classroom materials. Specialist kit reservations and digital accounts are VERIFICATION REQUIRED.
  • Keep projects small enough to test and assess in the native period. If a longer project is selected, label the meetings and storage/reset steps.
  • Use the audit's prep/cleanup estimates as planning estimates, not measured teacher timings. Time a first run and record improvements.
  • No routine homework. Family questions and activities are optional and do not supply evidence required for participation or mastery.

docs.title: Grade-band evidence
docs.text: Read the detailed K, 1-2, 3-4 and 5-6 reviews for exact track counts, original strengths/gaps, targeted revisions, remaining developmental concerns and unit newsletter snippets.

docs.title: Standards sources and implementation status
docs.text: Planning date and source access date: 2026-10-04. Target school year: 2026-27. All source entries record research on that date; the register distinguishes directly inspected text, indexed document references and failed retrievals. These are concise paraphrases, not reproductions of standards. Source years are edition labels; they are not necessarily adoption or implementation years.

docs.title: Classification and claim limits
docs.text:
• Official standard: Minnesota's adopted subject standards. Their public-school implementation dates are a reference for this Catholic school's planning, not a finding that every public-school accountability requirement applies here.
  • Official guidance/teaching: MDE implementation guidance; Archdiocesan guidance or policy; Vatican/USCCB teaching. These are not interchangeable with numbered academic benchmarks.
  • National standard/framework: CSTA, NGSS, National Core Arts Standards and ISTE. Use selectively; no Minnesota or Archdiocesan adoption is inferred.
  • Local program standard: The eighteen CST-* competencies in Local Standards. Not MDE-approved, not Archdiocese-approved, and not a complete subject curriculum.

Source verification does not establish lesson alignment. No external benchmark number is assigned to a lesson by this research. A claim requires the exact edition, applicable grade, verified benchmark, matching student task and assessment evidence. A topic resemblance or a local code is insufficient. All generated external-alignment fields remain VERIFICATION REQUIRED until that benchmark + lesson + individual assessment/evidence mapping is reviewed. A verified source, implementation date or local-code entry does not remove this hold.

docs.title: Minnesota: the 2026-27 baseline
docs.text:
The directly inspected MDE newsletters and enacted rules establish these dates. Older projected transition timelines must not override the later confirmations. docs.title: Archdiocese and OMCE
docs.text:
ID / classification Authoritative URL, accessed 2026-10-04 Concise finding and implementation status ARCH-01 / official office guidance Office for the Mission of Catholic Education Directly inspected page/HTML: OMCE provides vision, support and direction for teaching in the Church's name and forming disciples; Catholic schooling forms the whole student. It is not a numbered K-6 C-STREAM standards document. ARCH-02 / official Archdiocesan strategic guidance Educating children and young people for discipleship Directly inspected: connects faith throughout learning with the Roadmap for Excellence in Catholic Education and supports its implementation. This establishes the initiative, not a C-STREAM benchmark list. ARCH-03 / official Archdiocesan reporting of Roadmap guidance The Catholic Spirit: Roadmap work and OMCE changes The Archdiocese's newspaper reports the Roadmap launched in 2019, with work on governance, talent, curriculum/metrics, access/sustainability and mission schools. Historical strategic reporting; not a current subject-standard implementation mandate. ARCH-04 / official Archdiocesan reporting of current curriculum guidance The Catholic Spirit: integrated Catholic curriculum Directly inspected 2026 report attributes guidance to OMCE's curriculum specialist: religion/culture expectations released September 2025; schools expected to begin adopting recommended programs/curricula in 2026-27 and move toward full implementation over the following five years. Focus is elementary/middle school; K-8 leaders received training. This is reporting of guidance, not direct inspection of the full school-issued framework or a K-6 C-STREAM mandate. ARCH-05 / official policy and support entry points Policy Compendium; OMCE Mission Support Directly inspected: the compendium describes its policies as binding according to applicability; support page provides office resources. The full school-issued 2023 policy manual, integrated curriculum framework and sample five-year roadmap were not inspected. VERIFICATION REQUIRED for the school's applicable versions and obligations.

Bounded finding: Among the public office page, Roadmap references, official news reports, policy landing page and OMCE support listing inspected here, no detailed K-6 C-STREAM performance-standard/code catalog was located. This is not a claim that such standards do not exist. School-distributed, restricted, unindexed or subsequently published materials may exist. Ask the principal/OMCE for the current Integrated Catholic Curriculum for Religion and Culture, applicable school policies and any subject/C-STREAM standards before claiming Archdiocesan alignment or approval.

The four principles reported in ARCH-04 are academic achievement/integration, virtue formation/human development, spiritual life and apostolic discernment. They inform this program's philosophy; the eighteen local codes are not representations of an official OMCE code set.

docs.title: Catholic teaching: verified paragraph references
docs.text:
All paragraphs below were seen on the official Vatican site, including page HTML where the simplified reader omitted body text. Classroom applications are local interpretations of teaching, not official academic standards.

ID / classification Official URL and exact references, accessed 2026-10-04 Paraphrase / classroom application FAITH-01 / official Church teaching CCC: characteristics of faith, 159 Faith and reason are not rival sources of truth; legitimate scientific investigation need not contradict faith. Keep observations and explanations honest; do not use theology as an experimental result. FAITH-02 / official Church teaching CCC: the human person as God's image, 1702, 1704 Every person bears God's image; reason participates in understanding creation and seeking the good. Design for people's dignity and access, not their productivity or presumed ability. FAITH-03 / official Church teaching CCC: respect for personal dignity, 2293-2295 Science and technology serve human flourishing and are not morally neutral merely because they are efficient. Human experimentation has moral and consent limits. Classroom implication: safe models, privacy, no harmful experiments on classmates. FAITH-04 / official Church teaching CCC: persons and goods, 2415-2418 Respect creation and its resources, consider future generations, and avoid needless animal suffering. Reuse materials, minimize waste and observe living things responsibly. FAITH-05 / official Church teaching CCC: work and social justice, 2427-2428 Work proceeds from persons and can develop their gifts; people are not instruments of production. Value careful making, every honest vocation and service rather than speed or prestige. FAITH-06 / official Church teaching CCC: living in truth, 2468-2469 Truthfulness in actions and words sustains trust. Record actual results, acknowledge uncertainty and credit another person's idea.

USCCB inspection limit: The seven themes of Catholic social teaching and care for creation were attempted on 2026-10-04 but reliable text retrieval was blocked or incomplete. Their detailed wording and any proposed USCCB-specific citation are VERIFICATION REQUIRED. The applications above rest on the directly inspected Vatican paragraphs, not on unverified USCCB text.

docs.title: Optional national resources
docs.text:
ID / classification Authoritative URL(s), accessed 2026-10-04 Verified status, grade organization and permitted use NAT-01 / national CS standards CSTA 2026 PK-12 standards; published standards view; publisher's current 2026 PDF download; development history; current publication statement on the 2017 archive page 2026 edition is published, not merely a revision in progress. The currently retrieved archive page explicitly says publication was July 2026. The active viewer and actual PDF download independently establish a released edition, rather than a planned release inferred from an old announcement. Direct HTML inspection verifies PK/K combined, individual grades 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, middle school 6-8, high school 9-12. Grade 6 belongs to the middle-school band, not to a single-grade Grade 6 standard. Concepts include algorithms/design, programming, data/analysis, systems/security and computing/society. No local adoption date or complete CSTA alignment is asserted. NAT-02 / historical national CS standards CSTA 2017 interactive archive; original 2017 workbook Retain only explicitly 2017-labelled legacy mappings. Workbook directly verifies K-2, 3-5, 6-8 and 9-10 band labels; these must not be copied into the 2026 elementary structure. An inconsistent middle-level band label on the interactive page was resolved using the original workbook. No 2017 benchmark number is assigned to a lesson here. NAT-03 / national science/engineering framework and standards NGSS three-dimensional learning; NGSS topic arrangements Directly inspected: practices, crosscutting concepts and disciplinary core ideas work together; investigation asks explanatory questions, while engineering addresses design problems. Optional planning guidance, not an assertion that Minnesota adopted every NGSS performance expectation. Exact grade-band PE mapping is VERIFICATION REQUIRED before use. NAT-04 / national arts standards National Core Arts Standards Directly inspected page/HTML: creating, performing/presenting/producing, responding and connecting; includes visual arts and other arts. Optional guidance. Use MN-05 for Minnesota's edition and grade structure. No unseen national arts code or one-to-one equivalence is claimed. NAT-05 / national technology standards ISTE Standards for Students Directly inspected page/HTML: digital citizenship, research, design, computational thinking and communication are useful lenses. The site describes ongoing updates. Not Minnesota subject standards and not proof of CS programming proficiency; exact indicator/version mappings are VERIFICATION REQUIRED.

CSTA's pages describe attribution/noncommercial/share-alike licensing. This framework uses original local performance descriptions, not a reproduced or renumbered CSTA standards set. Check permissions before redistributing external standards text or publishing a derivative crosswalk.

Current-release check, 2026-10-04: The publisher's 2026 download returned HTTP 200, application/pdf, and a valid PDF header, resolving to its July 2026 hosted document. The live viewer offered the grade choices recorded in NAT-01. An older notice that a revision was scheduled for 2026 would not, by itself, support a claim of publication. The publication month here comes from the publisher's explicit past-tense statement, not just a URL date or the planning date.

docs.title: Legacy public-page claims: verification and safe wording
docs.text:
This ledger supports qualification of shared home/README pages and related resources. It does not approve their legacy attributions or change external lesson-alignment fields. The local eighteen-code framework and twelve design principles are not an NCEA standards set, an empirically validated intervention or a Cognia certification.

ID / classification Claim and primary-source status, researched 2026-10-04 Verification requirement and usable qualification LEGACY-01 / national Catholic education guidance; exact attribution unverified NCEA's ten characteristics of STREAM schools and claims of meeting "NCEA standards." The directly inspected NCEA Talk, STREAM in Action: Easy to Find is a contributed practitioner article about faith, service and STREAM, not the exact ten-item publication or a review of this curriculum. VERIFICATION REQUIRED for the original NCEA title, author, edition/date, exact list and any claimed correspondence. Do not use secondary lists as proof of NCEA's precise wording or numbering. Safe wording: local STREAM reflection checklist. Neither the article nor a checklist establishes NCEA approval, accreditation or program-wide alignment. LEGACY-02 / local design principles; research-validation claim unverified "Research-backed"/"research-based" twelve success factors, effectiveness claims and claims of demonstrated student outcomes. No baseline study set, claim-by-claim evidence synthesis or evaluation of this curriculum was supplied or verified. NAT-03 verifies science/engineering framework guidance, not the effectiveness of all twelve local principles or these lessons. VERIFICATION REQUIRED for each empirical claim: identifiable original research, applicable age/context, supported finding and limits, plus evidence for any claimed local outcome. Safe wording: local design principles informed by selected guidance. Do not call the program research-validated, proven effective or certified because a source describes its own framework as research-based. LEGACY-03 / national organizational certification guidance; local award/status unverified Cognia STEM certification/accreditation or conformity claims. The directly inspected current Cognia STEM certification page describes third-party evaluation and distinguishes institutional accreditation from STEM certification. Its FAQ says accreditation is not required to pursue STEM certification and describes certification as a six-year term. These are Cognia's current process descriptions, not findings about this school or repository. VERIFICATION REQUIRED for the named institution/program's award, issuer, scope and current term; obtain Cognia-issued evidence or a verified official status record. Separate accreditation from STEM certification. Exact standards-edition conformity also needs a reviewed crosswalk and evidence. Safe wording: Cognia offers a separate STEM certification process; this curriculum makes no certification or accreditation claim. A school's accreditation does not by itself establish STEM certification, and curriculum guidance is not an award. LEGACY-04 / training/material attribution unverified Steno training materials, attributed inspirational quotations and other unattributed source wording in legacy public pages. No exact original publication, author/date or training document was inspected for these claims. VERIFICATION REQUIRED before attributing exact wording, describing the materials as research evidence or implying provider endorsement. Use clearly identified local paraphrases/design commitments until the original source and appropriate attribution are established.

The NCEA article and Cognia process page are primary evidence only for what those pages actually describe. They do not establish that a historical ten-characteristic list matches the local checklist, that a provider's research validates this curriculum, or that the school has earned any credential. Unverified claims should be qualified or omitted, not converted into assertions that the publication, research or credential does not exist.

docs.title: Parent integration: remaining verification requirements
docs.text:
Autonomous follow-up, October 4: the state-agency 2018 workbook was downloaded and its K visual-arts/music rows inspected directly. Twelve source-verified K candidates use four exact identifiers, actual rewritten tasks and scoped individual evidence. The workbook's MDE-official-copy note and institutional review hold are retained. Normal math/science retrieval and integrated-browser reading did not provide readable final tables; the repealed 3501.0710 page and missing 3501.0970 page were not substituted for unseen current identifiers.

  1. Obtain the current final MDE benchmark documents through normal authorized access. Inspect each proposed K, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 row, its edition, full requirement and any coding notes. Science, math, ELA and social studies exact grade-table organization was not directly verified here. Do not publish guessed external benchmark IDs or copy older grade bands into a newer edition.
  2. Confirm the school's primary math edition for 2026-27 and any intentional early transition to 2022; keep implemented and transition mappings separate.
  3. Inspect MDE's current integrated CS collection and supporting guidance. Confirm all proposed subject/grade mappings and any newly enacted requirements. The inspected evidence does not substantiate a standalone CS framework deadline, nor automatic Minnesota adoption of the July 2026 CSTA publication.
  4. Obtain OMCE's school-issued religion/culture framework, policy manual and implementation roadmap. Verify school-specific expectations and any detailed C-STREAM standards not found in the inspected public sources.
  5. For every lesson claim, record source/edition, exact verified benchmark, applicable grade/band, task, individual assessment, success criterion and evidence location. An unplugged substitute cannot satisfy a requirement to operate or program a computing device merely by covering similar concepts.
  6. Mark unsupported crosswalk rows VERIFICATION REQUIRED. Complete subject coverage, diocesan approval, actual student mastery and classroom outcomes cannot be certified by this source review or the eighteen-code framework.
  7. Retain the LEGACY-01 through LEGACY-04 qualifications on shared public pages and downstream templates. Obtain the original NCEA/training publications, empirical evidence and current institution-specific Cognia award records before restoring stronger attribution, research or certification claims.

See Local Standards, Learning Progression and Philosophy for the local planning and assessment contract.

docs.title: Standards traceability and lesson map
docs.text:
• Download the complete lesson map.
  • Download local standards traceability.
  • Download lesson-to-material terms and reconciliation status.
  • Read source-verified K arts candidates.
  • Download the source-specific material reconciliation queue.
  • Read the local standards, learning progression and authoritative-source register.

docs.title: What a row means
docs.text:
Each traceability row connects a local program standard -> grade band -> schedule and rotation -> unit -> lesson -> planned assessment evidence. Filter the CSV by local_standard, grade_band, rotation and schedule. For example, filter CST-E2, 3-4, A, Weekly to find build/test/redesign opportunities and the evidence a teacher should collect.

The combined-grade row does not imply identical expectations for both grades. Use the grade-specific performance descriptions in the progression and the support/challenge guidance in the lesson. Students may enter either rotation; introduce required procedures and vocabulary before increasing independence.

The audit's status records the baseline disposition, while revision records subsequent changes. A lesson marked REBUILD and rebuilt has been revised; a baseline concern is not erased from the change record. improved is not a substitute-readiness certification. Read the band review and the actual lesson before scheduling.

These are editorial alignment judgments about intended student work. They are not evidence that a class has mastered a standard. A general exit check may support only part of a competency; teachers must collect the individual performance evidence specified in the local progression.

docs.title: Material queries
docs.text:
Filter the material-usage CSV by grade_band, schedule and rotation to see what the selected lessons name. item_id connects an exact canonical/alias name to the normalized inventory. This is text matching only, not verified item specifications, quantity sufficiency, ownership or safety. Unmatched and ambiguous terms are retained visibly for reconciliation rather than assigned an invented substitute. The inventory's verified-use count remains separate from these textual occurrences.

The reconciliation queue groups remaining occurrences by exact term, grade and source lesson, with an explicit follow-up reason. A suggested triage category is not a supplier/item equivalence: software/access, record formats, quantity phrases, ambiguous adhesives and safety-critical parts still need their actual lesson specifications. It is a work queue, not a purchase list.

docs.title: Official standards claim gate
docs.text:
Every generated external-alignment field is VERIFICATION REQUIRED. This is intentional, not a substitute for the source research. An official claim needs all of the following:

  1. Applicable adopted/implemented version and school year.
  2. Verified exact benchmark identifier, grade and source URL/document.
  3. Student action that actually practices the benchmark.
  4. Specific assessment evidence for the relevant part of the benchmark.
  5. Reviewer/date and any scope limitations.

A topic resemblance, Catholic quotation, tag, device, or project photograph does not establish official alignment. This enrichment program does not replace the school's science, mathematics, arts, ELA, social studies or religion curricula.

docs.title: Updating and validating
docs.text:
The four band-audit CSVs are the source of the combined maps. From the repository root in PowerShell:

.\scripts\Build-CurriculumMaps.ps1
.\scripts\Build-CurriculumMaps.ps1 -ValidateOnly
mkdocs build

For the current K version-3.0 reference set, update lesson metadata and the individual-evidence definitions together, then run .\scripts\Sync-KindergartenAudit.ps1 and .\scripts\Test-KindergartenReferences.ps1 before regenerating the maps. The K validator checks 29 autonomous references/37 native meetings, class-size arithmetic and complete audit evidence; it does not approve physical kits or certify learning outcomes.

The script fails explicitly on missing or duplicate lessons, invalid schema/enums, schedule/rotation mismatches, wrong period lengths, missing evidence fields and unknown local standard codes. It also verifies that every lesson file appears exactly once and all 18 codes exist in the catalog. It checks inventory identifier uniqueness and nonnegative prices/quantities, and produces a material-term index without guessing unresolved matches. -ValidateOnly also rejects missing or stale generated maps; run generation after editing the source audits or inventory and include those maps in the change. It does not infer official alignment, substitute usability, safety, developmental appropriateness or classroom mastery from a passing schema.

docs.title: Substitute readiness review
docs.text:
October 2026. A revised template is not certification of every lesson. This workstream owns shared operations, not the four band lesson audits. Readiness requires a completed lesson, counted physical kit, accommodations, named local contact and successful prep test. Classroom outcomes, inventory condition, staff availability and school policies remain unverified.

Evidence status: The seven simulations below are planned desk walk-throughs of documents and assumptions. No substitute-arrival trial, pupil classroom test, observed teacher-prep timing or actual kit-capacity trial was performed. Future READY status requires the named local checks; it is not an outcome already established by this review.

docs.title: What changed in shared operations
docs.text: Baseline problems: the old substitute guide assumed nonexistent quick-reference cards and "likely" equipment locations, treated paper as an equivalent for programming, and had no complete classroom cleanup/evidence allocation. The updated substitute guide supplies the actual 20-minute gate, native-period fallback plans and safety escalation. The handoff template attaches a complete lesson plan, not a second format. Shared kits and actual stock assumptions live in Materials Plan.

docs.title: Grade 3, twenty minutes before class
docs.text:
Use this actual target, maintained by the band owner: Week 10: Bridge Engineering. Use the rebuilt lesson's exact span, loads, issue quantities and individual check; the generic structures kit is not permission to change those silently. Do not read its old title as proof of readiness.

Preparation window Substitute action Evidence of readiness 0-4 minutes Read the linked lesson's at-a-glance objective, background, misconception and 40-minute sequence Can state the objective and individual success condition 4-8 Locate the labeled kit and count actual enrollment; this bridge uses 12 active pair/trio teams at 25, with a 13-kit supply budget 26 books, 28 paper sheets, 260 identical counters, 13 cups/trays/team rulers, 5.2 m tape, 25 evidence slips and the specified teacher reserves are present 8-12 Review safety/accommodations; confirm office contact/stop procedure; inspect supports and loads No damaged/sharp/loose unsafe items; no hidden teacher-only task 12-16 Run the lesson's prep test and prepare trays/roles Test result is observable; setup can be safely supervised 16-20 Draw/read aloud steps; rehearse one exit prompt, return counts and fallback Individual roster and 40-minute cleanup/evidence allocation ready

If the exact kit/pretest is unavailable, explicitly teach the paper comparison fallback in the substitute guide instead. Tell the regular teacher which bridge objectives/evidence were deferred. The nine-team generic structures kit is not the complete pair-based bridge kit. The fallback uses groups of up to three and its own quantities and test, so record the changed objective rather than silently changing the bridge's span, loading method or team allocation. Do not add unsourced theological metaphors, ratio mathematics or unfamiliar electric equipment to rescue a lesson.

Readiness states: READY after local checks; CONDITIONAL with a named, tested support/fallback; NOT READY with unresolved safety, material, instruction or assessment blockers. The link and a document simulation do not establish school-wide READY status.

docs.title: Seven desk simulations (not classroom trials)
docs.text: Simulation Shared resources tested conceptually Outcome and limit 1. Substitute arrives 20 minutes before Grade 3 Linked rebuilt bridge target + gate above + structures kit/fallback Feasible only after actual kit/count/pretest; no blanket legacy certification 2. K child cannot read Show, Try, Tell, real objects, one modeled step and pointing/gesture No reading/writing prerequisite; teacher still records each child's concept evidence 3. iPads unavailable Technology Plan separates no-device concepts from execution Core works; software/robot execution deferred and NE, never programming mastery from paper 4. Minnesota January, -10 F Indoor desk observation, paper engineering, classroom comparison No outdoor exposure needed; a weather-specific outdoor objective requires a different approved lesson 5. Enrollment 25 Generic core: nine teams up to three; revised pair-based bridge: 12 active teams plus one reserve kit; seated work and 25 response opportunities Use the selected lesson's count, not one universal kit count; actual supplies and room layout still need checking 6. Budget ceiling $250 Goods $194 + tax $15.52 + shipping $10 + durable reserve $10 = $229.52 Hands-on low-tech core plus protected AA equipment; one cohort and existing basics assumed, not all legacy lessons 7. Parent asks what learning occurred Unit copy, objective-linked rubric, actual evidence and Catholic decision Teacher can give concept/action/evidence/next step; family tasks remain optional

docs.title: Required local checks before handoff
docs.text:
• Verify school contact/emergency arrangements, accommodations and actual kit shelf locations; this review invents none.
  • Verify protected electrical ratings, secure covers, age suitability, ingredients and counts. No button cells, latex balloons or projectiles; no neodymium magnets in K. Suspected battery/magnet ingestion requires immediate school emergency escalation.
  • Confirm the current rebuilt bridge instructions and physical kit agree. Band audits record document-level revision evidence, not classroom testing or official certification; this operations review does not replace them.
  • Reconcile the four available audit CSVs by lesson path; record substitute/safety/technology blockers. The Grade 3 band owner has documented the rebuilt bridge reference and conservative 13-kit supply budget; verify the actual local kit rather than using the earlier as-read snapshot. The audit is not classroom certification. Do not infer that all 251 legacy documents are ready because the template exists.
  • Check Local Standards definitions, faith sources and official alignment; unverified Church or supplier claims are VERIFICATION REQUIRED.

The substitute leaves actual individual evidence/NE, accomplished steps, objective changes, missing/broken supplies, safety issues and follow-up questions.

docs.title: Technology plan
docs.text: October 2026. Technology includes tools, systems, algorithms, input/output and ethical decisions, not only screens. Computer science is not synonymous with consuming an app. Actual school accounts, licenses, privacy approvals, device counts, Wi-Fi and loan availability are VERIFICATION REQUIRED.

docs.title: Four requirement labels
docs.text:
Label Meaning Appropriate example None No digital device needed for the stated objective Observe/model/measure; compose a body-percussion phrase; follow and debug a paper algorithm Optional Device changes convenience, not the demonstrated objective Teacher photographs a model instead of drawing; optional document camera with real-object demonstration alternative Recommended Device adds educational value but the same objective can still be evidenced without it Large data set graphing when a manageable paper data set preserves the taught interpretation criterion Required Stated objective cannot be demonstrated without the actual digital/programmable device Run/debug a Scratch program; operate a programmed robot or sensor; test an interactive input controller

Each lesson names the device/app version, compatible access, why it is needed, quantity/turns, prep test and fallback. Electricity using protected AA packs does not require a screen. Digital art is not the only arts route: observational drawing, model form, composition, rhythm and performance are authentic A.

docs.title: Objective-preserving vs objective-changing alternatives
docs.text:
Learning purpose Usual label No-device route Evidence limit Sequence, loops, conditions, decomposition, debugging concepts None Large arrow cards, desk grids, repeated actions or sorting rules Evidence of computational thinking; not proof that software executed Closed path/input-output in simple circuits None Preflight-approved Snap Circuits in selected OLP lessons, or the separate protected-AA route Paper circuit diagram alone does not prove building/testing an electrical circuit Science observation, temperature, structures, measurement None Physical objects, non-glass tools, individual show/tell/data A teacher demo alone does not evidence every student's investigation Observation/composition/pattern/music objective None or Optional Paper design and sound/silence phrase with body percussion If objective specifically concerns a digital tool, paper changes it Evidence documentation/presentation Optional Draw/label/model/orally explain Personal recording devices are not prerequisites Research/data interpretation Recommended only with justification Teacher-vetted printed/text read-aloud source; small supplied data set Online source-evaluation objective requires appropriate actual online examples/access Scratch/ScratchJr executable program Required Plan/trace/debug on paper now; schedule executable program later Mark execution objective NE/deferred; never record programming mastery from paper Dash/Sphero/Ozobot or sensor-controlled behavior Required Predict/trace algorithm using pointer on grid Robot operation, sensing and live debugging require working compatible equipment later Standalone stored-program floor robot Required for execution Large paper sequence while unit is unavailable Optional enhanced purchase; no host assumed only after product verification USB input/Makey Makey/modular app-linked project Required where digital response is O1 Draw input/output model or use AA circuit for a different O1 Different objective explicitly recorded; proprietary power components never improvised

If the technology fails: try the lesson's pretested basic restart/connection steps briefly, then protect teaching time and switch to a named fallback. Do not create personal accounts, bypass protections, install unknown software or download unapproved materials during class. Record what objective changed, what was actually demonstrated and when the missing evidence will be collected.

docs.title: Access, capacity and sustainability
docs.text:
Default maximum team size three: 10/15/20/25 pupils need ⅘/7/9 working team devices. Each student needs an execution/debugging turn for individual evidence. If there are only four devices for 25, plan nine teams in three rotations, each with a specified test/reset time and meaningful non-device work; schedule additional meetings if native 25/30/40/45 minutes cannot include every turn, assessment and cleanup. Do not equate watching another group with mastery. Account accessibility and sensory/motor supports must be confirmed.

The materials budgets fund no managed tablet/computer or licensed app. Enhanced robots are a conditional option, not a promise of Dash/Sphero/EV3 availability. HOST/DASH/SPHERO/MODULAR/INPUT database rows are legacy inventory questions. Verify loan contents, dates, chargers, missing pieces, age ratings, host compatibility, app availability/support and all fees before selecting a device-dependent lesson.

docs.title: Before any app or online service
docs.text:
Verification required Responsible school role to assign Evidence to retain locally Existing managed device count/condition, chargers, compatible OS [Technology lead] Asset count and dated trial Cost/free license terms, education eligibility, offline capability [Purchasing/technology lead] Current vendor terms and tested function Age terms, accounts, data collected, retention/deletion, consent [Administrator/privacy lead] Actual approval under school policy Access restrictions, advertisements, public sharing and accessibility [Teacher/technology lead] Classroom configuration and fallback Student images/names/work and family permission [School-approved contact] Verified school consent process, not assumed consent Loan inventory and return/transportation terms [Loan coordinator] Confirmed booking, complete kit and dates

Scratch, ScratchJr, Code.org, Chrome Music Lab, Canva, Tinkercad and robot apps are legacy candidates, not guaranteed free/approved/installed services. Use current vendor information for verification; this plan creates no school account or privacy policy. No student data are uploaded as part of this review.

docs.title: All-grade audit reconciliation
docs.text:
The final October 4 integration of all four band audits classifies 251 document records as 149 None, 49 Optional, 15 Recommended, 38 Required. K has 0 Required; grades 1-2 have 10, grades 3-4 have 17 and grades 5-6 have 11. These are primary-path audit labels, not meeting counts, ownership or readiness certifications. Protected AA circuit materials remain required even when the digital-technology label is None. Use the generated lesson map for subsequent updates.

Use actual paths, schedules and rotations to connect material/host questions. Keep objective-preserving and objective-changing fallback fields distinct. Recorded devices/kit names indicate procurement questions, not ownership, approval or safe equivalent substitution. Confirm Ozobot/EV3/other proprietary platforms separately rather than pricing them as the generic floor robot. App/device inventory, licenses and all-lesson readiness remain unverified; this workstream does not reread assigned band lessons or infer holdings from names.

OLP Snap follow-up: the school confirmed eight individual activity kits, not classroom packs. The classroom guide documents four selected lesson pathways, matching-model/age/power gates, five-station/two-wave access at 25 pupils and separate physical/paper evidence. Snap's slide switch uses two states repeated twice; it does not establish the protected-AA push-button route's four independently controlled states. No computer/app is added, and no unverified holder equivalence is claimed.

Operational entry points: library planning, substitute guide, lesson template. Standards claims use Local Standards; official alignment requires verification.

docs.title: Final consistency checks and seven classroom simulations
docs.text: Date: October 4, 2026. Evidence type: document inspection, structured-data checks, arithmetic and desk walkthroughs. No actual substitute-arrival trial, classroom pilot, physical-kit inspection or student-outcome study was performed.

docs.title: Persistent outputs and automated checks
docs.text:
• 251 lessons: each existing weekly/bi-weekly lesson file appears exactly once in the 19-field audit/combined lesson map.
  • 807 local-standard evidence links: valid codes, grade bands, schedule/ rotation paths, nonblank evidence, native periods and positive meeting counts.
  • 18 local competencies: all catalog codes present; grade progression contains 126 planned performance targets and 126 instructional-stage entries.
  • 74 inventory items: unique identifiers, nonnegative decimal prices and integer class-size quantities. The generated index retains 1,203 lesson/material terms, including visible unresolved name/specification questions. It does not claim all legacy materials are procurement-ready. 727 occurrences have exact canonical/alias name matches; 476 occurrences require reconciliation. Even a matched name still needs specification and quantity verification.
  • 72 rebuilt, 167 improved, 12 unchanged lesson documents: baseline disposition/priority remains separate from the revision state.
  • Regression checks: valid synthetic map generation and ten rejection cases passed, including duplicate/missing lessons, invalid codes, wrong periods, missing evidence, invalid labels/rotations/paths/meeting counts and stale generated maps. Fixtures and logs remain session artifacts, not curriculum.
  • Budget checks (pre-Snap record): independently joined 37 bill-of-material rows to the expanded 68-item inventory; only the original selected purchase rows are included. First-year totals are $229.52 / $476.04 / $854.32 / $2,367.84, below the four stated ceilings. Nine generic teams provide capacity 27, but pair-based reference lessons use their own larger kit counts.
  • Source checks: implementation dates and release status are documented separately from exact official lesson alignment, which remains VERIFICATION REQUIRED.

docs.title: Autonomous Kindergarten follow-up
docs.text:
• All 37 K documents are complete conditional references after rebuilding the remaining 29. The six former audit-only checks are now implemented.
  • New-reference validation covers 37 native meeting sequences and 360 class-size quantity comparisons, with baseline judgments/paths/meetings/ minutes unchanged. These are document/arithmetic checks, not observed timings.
  • Every K primary-material term has a catalog match; global unresolved terms were 501 occurrences at K closeout, down from the initial 750. The term population also changed as compound K lists were decomposed, so this is not a count of 249 verified physical items.
  • The reconciliation queue groups those originally grouped those 501 occurrences into 241 exact terms with grade/source paths and an explicit follow-up reason; it is not a purchase list.
  • Dated weather comparisons, requested book criteria/tradeoffs and hypothetical privacy/adult-help checks close concrete progression gaps without extra periods.
  • Twelve source-verified arts candidates connect four exact identifiers to eleven lessons. MDE-copy corroboration and school review remain required; science/math identifiers were not guessed.
  • The existing report of 8 OHM-135 Snap Circuits kits is retained in a separate holdings record, not treated as inspected stock or a purchase bill.
  • Test-KindergartenReferences.ps1 is wired into publication CI alongside map validation; the practical K routines and source-candidate page are included in site navigation.

docs.title: Bounded OLP Snap Circuits follow-up
docs.text:
Four existing Grades 3-6 lessons now use eight individual reported OHM-135 activity kits; ownership is not completed physical inspection. The shared guide requires matching model/manual, age, battery-access/protection and school approval checks. No guessed project number, cell allocation, sensor or push-button behavior is substituted for the matching instructions.

The dedicated Test-SnapCircuitsReferences.ps1 checks four retained paths, six contiguous native meeting sequences, 20 station/capacity rows, the eight-kit holding, baseline status/priority, physical/paper evidence boundaries, relative links and guide navigation. At 25 pupils, nine teams use five stations in two 12-minute (Grades 3-4) or 14-minute (Grades 5-6) waves; no group exceeds three. These are document/arithmetic checks, not observed classroom timing or kit safety certification. Protected-AA routes remain separate alternatives.

The current maps contain 807 local-code links and 1,203 material occurrences: 727 exact catalog name matches and 476 unresolved occurrences across 237 terms. Snap stock is in the separate holdings record; its unresolved priced-catalog term does not mean no school stock or authorize a zero-price purchase row. Shared purchase totals are unchanged.

Snap follow-up results: PASS. Four lesson references, six contiguous native meetings, 20 capacity rows and ten relative links passed the dedicated check; the regenerated 251-lesson maps passed -ValidateOnly against the current 74-item catalog. MkDocs built successfully with only the previously recorded README/index conflict warning. These results do not release kit preflight gates.

docs.title: Seven required simulations
docs.text: Simulation Concrete walkthrough and improvement Result and required local checks 1. Grade 3 substitute arrives 20 minutes before class Bridge Engineering has a 40-minute sequence, background, fair-test directions, individual evidence and cleanup. The handoff supplies a 20-minute prep gate. Integration corrected its mismatch with the generic nine-team kit: budget 13 kits for 12 active teams at 25, 26 books, 260 counters, 28 sheets and 5.2 m tape. Conditional document pass: feasible with the prepared counted kit. Actual location, supplies, room, accommodations and pretest must be confirmed. Otherwise use the explicitly different fallback and record deferred objectives. 2. Kindergarten child cannot read Movement/picture algorithms uses modeled arrows, large paper pieces, pointing/moving and oral evidence; Show, Try, Tell supports nonwritten responses. Document pass for the reference pathway: independent reading/handwriting is not required. The teacher still checks each child's reasoning and gives the third child a full turn. 3. iPads unavailable Technology plan and actual lesson alternatives separate computational reasoning from digital execution. Current labels: 149 None, 49 Optional, 15 Recommended, 38 Required. Approved Snap/protected-AA circuit routes need no computing device but retain physical-material gates. Conditional program pass: the documented low-tech core continues. Real programming, robot/sensor operation and digital-tool objectives requiring devices are deferred, not falsely awarded from paper or teacher demonstration. 4. Minnesota January, -10 F K picture grids/indoor observation, paper bridge tests, the indoor weather reference and fictional paper evidence require no outdoor exposure. Prepared/simulated data are labeled. Document pass for selected indoor pathways: authentic outdoor measurements cannot be claimed from simulated data; move or explicitly change such objectives. Live plant care and indoor wet-work cleanup need local planning. 5. Enrollment rises to 25 Exact reference tables, roles, seated testing and individual roster sweeps replace serial queues. Generic groups <=3 need nine kits; pair-based references retain larger budgets. The selected Snap routes use nine teams/five stations/two waves within the native meeting. Conditional capacity pass: arithmetic and written logistics cover 25. Use the exact selected pathway, not a universal kit count. Physical space, stock, inspection throughput and observed individual turns remain untested. 6. Limited funding Starter plan totals $229.52 with supplies, tax/shipping/contingency estimates and no required devices, specialty loans or donations. Existing school basics and one-cohort consumables are explicit. Conditional budget pass: prices/specifications and stock are estimates. This is a modest low-tech core, not purchase coverage for all 251 legacy lessons or all pair-based references. Safe electrical procurement may not be improvised to preserve a price. 7. Parent asks what the child learns Family system, band unit snippets, scope, progression and traceability connect concepts/actions, Catholic reasoning, planned evidence and next steps. The forensic reference makes truth/dignity concrete without accusing anyone. Document pass: a teacher can explain a selected lesson and its progression in plain language. Describe actual evidence gathered; never imply that planned targets or group participation prove mastery. Home invitations are optional.

docs.title: Weaknesses exposed and corrected during integration
docs.text:
1. Unit totals had been stored as per-meeting minutes in some audits. All rows now use native 25/30/40/45 minutes; meetings * minutes gives duration.
  2. Shared substitute guidance used a nine-team kit for a pair-based bridge. The handoff now uses the exact conservative 13-kit supply budget.
  3. Protected AA circuits were inconsistently counted as requiring digital technology. Labels now distinguish digital needs from required physical materials; electrical mastery still requires an actual safely tested circuit.
  4. A Grades 1-2 bridge table needed an explicit odd-enrollment arrangement. A final trio and reserve kit are specified, with individual role rotation.
  5. Outside-document script links in band reviews were replaced with the published traceability guide and an inline command.
  6. The operations snapshot was stale after lesson revisions. Materials and technology summaries now use the integrated audit counts and generated maps.
  7. Exact-name material matching exposed unresolved terms. They remain visible for reconciliation; no invented quantities, prices or equivalent items are silently supplied.

docs.title: Remaining release conditions
docs.text:
The band reviews record unresolved instructional/source/operational holds. An improved file is not a full reference rebuild; a full document is not a classroom certification. Hold unresolved P0 pathways and finish the next scheduled P1 lesson before teaching.

Before calling the program uniformly classroom-ready, confirm actual stock, protected electrical specifications, supplier prices, school safety/privacy/ account rules, accommodations, source-gated history/Church claims, applicable official benchmark mapping and physical kit locations. Pilot scheduled lessons, time preparation/cleanup, gather individual evidence on the local mastery checkpoints and revise using those observations.

K has zero remaining document-package holds. Its physical/school/source gates and classroom trials remain; the other three bands' documented readiness queues were not silently closed by the autonomous K work.

docs.title: C-STREAM rubrics
docs.text:
October 2026 revision: lightweight ¾-level evidence rather than universal 100-point weighting. State the objective, prompt and Meets condition first. NE = not yet evidenced, not a zero or proof of low mastery.

Need Resource Audience Project science/design/math/arts evidence Student project rubric Teacher/student; each child demonstrates learning Reasoning, communication or taught collaboration skill Skills assessment Teacher; observable actions, not personality Taught dignity/service/stewardship reasoning Service rubric Teacher/student; no compulsory external service Quality/accuracy of faith integration in a lesson Faith-reason rubric Teacher/administrator; NOT a student belief score Write a specific criterion Rubric template Lesson author; three or four levels Record each child's evidence Assessment template Teacher; prompt, evidence, feedback, next check

Assessment measures the stated objective, not participation, handwriting, neatness, presentation expense or confidence. An arts criterion assesses a named composition/design/performance skill only if taught as an objective. Accept show/tell/draw/scribe/record with access supports. Failed models can provide excellent evidence; a working group product does not establish every child's mastery. Never grade prayer habits, family religion or interior belief.

Use the 18 local codes with actual lesson evidence. Official standards/Church quotation claims require source verification. Do not equate a rubric score with complete official curriculum alignment.

docs.title: Thinking, communication and collaboration assessment
docs.text:
The earlier question banks on reasoning, communication, collaboration, creativity, curiosity and ethics remain useful purposes. Select an explicitly taught objective, not a universal character score. October 2026.

Taught objective 1 Beginning 2 Developing 3 Meets Expectation 4 Extends Learning Justify a design choice with evidence Choice contradicts observed evidence Gives a relevant choice but evidence link is incomplete Explains the choice with the specified observed result Compares an alternative using another result or tradeoff Communicate a result Response does not yet convey the result Conveys part of the result Shows/tells/draws the result and relevant evidence clearly enough to interpret Adapts explanation after a clarifying question without changing the evidence Combine two ideas in a plan (only if an objective) Plan does not yet include either discussed idea Uses one idea, or includes both without explaining their use Identifies each idea and shows how they contribute to the plan Tests the combined plan and explains an improvement based on feedback Revise an artistic/design idea Change is unrelated to the purpose Relevant revision with an incomplete explanation Revises a taught visual/musical/design choice and explains its purpose Compares versions and explains an intentional effect or tradeoff Frame an investigable question Question cannot yet be investigated with the available evidence Question is relevant but too broad States a question answerable by the planned observation/test Refines it using results and identifies what to test next Explain a privacy/stewardship choice Does not yet recognize the taught concern Names the concern without linking the action Explains how a concrete choice addresses the taught concern Compares two actions and explains consequences for people/resources

NE is not yet evidenced. Teacher read-aloud, bilingual response, gesture, scribe and motor assistance are access supports, not evidence of a lower level. Do not score smiles, spontaneous awe, public speaking confidence, written fluency, leadership, speed or active participation as subject mastery. Behavior/engagement can be noted separately for support planning without converting it into the objective's grade.

docs.title: Faith-reason integration lesson-quality rubric
docs.text: Audience: teachers/administrators, not a student faith score. October 2026. Preserves the earlier focus on faith/reason, Catholic teaching, wonder, heritage and service while avoiding a compulsory saint/Scripture/prayer formula for every lesson. C shapes the purpose and choices; R is explicit faith teaching/reflection. Scientific inquiry remains evidence-based.

docs.title: Local planning criteria
docs.text:
Lesson-quality criterion 1 Beginning 2 Developing 3 Meets Expectation 4 Extends Quality Faith and empirical reasoning distinguished Religious claim presented as experimental proof, or science misstated Connection named but distinction unclear Scientifically accurate evidence and Catholic reflection distinguished Teacher background anticipates a misconception and models a careful source/evidence response Catholic purpose affects work No connection or prayer alone General value named without a classroom decision Students consider a specific dignity, stewardship, truth or service choice Choice is revisited using results, user needs or a tradeoff Source accuracy Invented/misattributed standard, quotation or Church claim Source question marked but not yet resolved Primary source checked, quoted/paraphrased accurately and linked Appropriate context and limits are explained in teacher-friendly language Inquiry and wonder Questions suppressed or inquiry replaced by a craft Wonder question named but no student investigation Students observe/ask/test and reflect without forced theological inference New student questions guide a feasible next investigation Access and evidence Participation/prayer behavior graded as belief Flexible modes named but criteria unclear Named objective assessed with individual oral/drawn/model/written evidence Results inform specific access support and next teaching

Mark optional heritage/service extensions N/A if not relevant to that lesson; do not add points for more quotations, longer prayers or named scientists. Record dimension evidence, not a /20 total suggesting official certification. Unresolved source accuracy is a readiness blocker, not a minor score offset.

Source pathway: Local Standards and the shared review's authoritative source record. A primary reference for faith/reason is Fides et Ratio. VERIFICATION REQUIRED for exact passage/quotation and any claimed diocesan or state requirement. This rubric is local, not an official Church standard.

docs.text:
1. Write grade/unit/lesson, objective O1/O2, individual prompt and success condition using Assessment Template.
  2. Select 1-3 relevant criteria below; adjust Meets to the lesson's exact measurable threshold and grade prerequisites before teaching.
  3. Link the defined local standard. Official alignment requires verification, not a claim that a score meets all standards.
  4. Share expectations by showing/telling students. Offer oral, model, drawing, scribed or written evidence. Team products support, but never replace, each child's demonstration.

docs.title: Four levels
docs.text:
Objective-linked criterion (use only if taught) 1 Beginning 2 Developing 3 Meets Expectation 4 Extends Learning O1 scientific observation/comparison Describes an outcome inconsistent with what was observed Names a relevant observation but comparison is incomplete Makes the specified comparison using an observed result Repeats or transfers the comparison and explains supporting evidence O1 fair test/engineering redesign Changes conditions without recognizing their effect Tests and suggests a change but evidence link is incomplete Uses the stated common conditions, records a result and justifies one redesign Retests the redesign and compares performance or a tradeoff using evidence O2 measurement/math reasoning Quantity/unit or comparison is incorrect Partly correct measure/data with a specific error remaining Measures/represents/explains using the lesson's specified quantity and unit Checks the result or uses it to justify a new comparison O2 algorithm/programming Sequence cannot produce intended result Sequence partly works; bug or execution evidence remains unresolved Explains/tests the intended sequence; real execution included if objective requires it Finds and tests a new correction/condition and explains the effect O2 artistic communication/music Chosen form/pattern does not yet convey the stated idea Artistic choice partly conveys the idea/phrase Uses the stated visual or musical choice to communicate the intended idea/phrase Revises a composition/phrase after feedback and explains the artistic effect O2 Catholic/ethical/service reasoning Choice does not yet address the taught dignity/stewardship principle Names the principle or user but connection to choice is incomplete Explains a concrete choice and how it respects the taught principle/user need Compares two choices and explains an evidence-informed tradeoff in light of the principle

NE = not yet evidenced, outside the scale. Missed observation, absence, device failure or an inaccessible response mode is not Beginning. Access supports do not cap levels. A conceptual hint is recorded separately. Artistic skill is scored only for an explicit arts objective; handwriting, neatness, beautiful displays, expensive boards, confident speech, participation and family assistance are not mastery criteria. No grades for interior faith, prayer frequency, family religious practice or apparent enthusiasm.

docs.title: Individual score/evidence record
docs.text:
Student Objective/local code Actual response/action Mode/access support Level or NE Feedback and next check [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ]

Do not average unrelated objectives into a pseudo-precise total. Report "Compared two bridge tests using the same span; next, explain the redesign" instead of "earned 80%, meets all C-STREAM standards." Expected-mastery checkpoints follow Local Standards: two dated observations on separate occasions, including an individual demonstration and changed context/follow-up explanation, both meeting the target. One project rating does not establish end-of-grade mastery.

docs.title: Bridge example and moderation
docs.text:
O1: Compare two paper designs under the same span/load conditions. Meets: child names the observed result and shows which conditions stayed the same. A failed prototype can provide successful learning evidence. A team's strong bridge with no individual explanation is NE for that child's comparison. Drawings can communicate the comparison without handwriting assessment.

Before a showcase, two teachers score the same anonymized examples using the selected criteria and resolve discrepancies. Events are optional celebrations of in-school work; a child's assessment does not depend on home construction, family attendance or purchased display materials.

docs.title: Show, Try, Tell
docs.text:
Teacher/substitute: This is an adult-led card, not independent reading. Use it with the actual lesson objective and kit. A printed copy is optional. Draw the three boxes on the board or place three real objects as visual cues. Say ONE step, show it, let the child do it, then repeat. No homework.

docs.title: Ready-to-use comparison example (K/nonreader)
docs.text:
Objective: "I can show which of two objects is longer." Materials: Two ordinary school pencils of visibly different lengths, each child's familiar drawing tool/paper optional. No small new parts or devices.

  1. Hold up the two pencils. Say "Look." Put them side by side with ends aligned.
  2. Model pointing along a pencil. Say "Show the longer one." Let each child point.
  3. Reverse left/right order, realign ends. Say "Show me again. How do you know?" Accept tracing, pointing at the unmatched end, gesture or words; adult scribes.

Meets: Child identifies the longer pencil in both placements and indicates the unmatched end/aligned comparison. If position alone determines the answer, model aligned ends and recheck later. Do not score reading, handwriting or speech. This is a local classroom criterion, not a verified official benchmark.

Support: Larger objects, extra wait time, adult holds objects steady, child uses gaze/gesture or home-language response. Challenge: Compare a third object and explain the order. Catholic connection: Care for shared tools and use them fairly; no scientific proof claim or forced comparison of God to an engineer. Safety: No sharpening/swinging; keep tools at desk level.

All required work and supplies are provided at school; no routine homework or donation prerequisites.

Creating... Use What it protects One meeting Lesson plan At a glance, background/vocabulary, native timings, safety, scaling and individual evidence A unit Cross-curricular unit Prerequisites, meeting sequence, balance, logistics, family copy Multi-meeting project PBL overlay Launch/research/create/present using the same unit and lesson formats Student response Student sheet Show/tell/draw or record; nonreader route Substitute handoff Substitute lesson 20-minute preparation gate and named fallbacks Individual evidence Assessment Objective -> prompt -> success condition -> student evidence ¾-level criteria Rubric Observable objective-linked levels, not participation or polish Family copy Newsletter Actual learning and optional no-purchase conversation/activity Materials/kit Materials list Normalized items, 10/15/20/25 quantities and replenishment Standards evidence Standards mapping Local catalog and separately verified official alignment

The local 18-code catalog defines CST-C1..C3, CST-S1..S3, CST-T1..T3, CST-E1..E3, CST-A1..A3 and CST-M1..M3. Do not generate new local codes or label these official Archdiocesan/Minnesota standards. Official source questions remain VERIFICATION REQUIRED.

Operational entry points: materials, technology, substitutes, family communication, rubrics, student resources.

docs.title: Assessment template
docs.text:
Grade/unit/lesson/date: [ ] Objective O1: [Observable action + concept + condition.] Local code: [From Local Standards.]

Objective Actual individual prompt/task Success condition When/how collected Allowed mode/support O1 "[Question]" / [Demonstration] [Number, unit, correct comparison, evidence or explanation required] [During test/exit; minutes] [Show/tell/draw/scribe/record]

Example, not an official grade benchmark: O1 compare two paper structures under the same load. Prompt: "Show which held the load, and what stayed the same in your test." Meets: identifies the observed result and keeps span/load placement the same. A failed bridge can supply valid evidence.

Student Actual evidence, not "good work" Objective Level ½/¾ or NE Access support Feedback/next check [ ] [ ] O1 [ ] [ ] [ ]

Use Rubric Template. NE means not yet evidenced; absence, missed observation or equipment failure does not prove low mastery. Ordinary access accommodations do not cap a score. Distinguish a conceptual hint from read-aloud, translation, scribing or motor assistance.

Collect a response from every child; a group prototype is supporting evidence, not an individual score. At 25, observe nine teams during hands-on work plus simultaneous exit responses. Mark any unobserved child NE and arrange a brief next-meeting check. Give one specific feedback statement and one next action. Do not average unrelated objectives or replace learning evidence with participation, prayer behavior, confidence or attractive displays.

Expected-mastery checkpoints: Follow Local Standards: at least two dated observations on separate occasions, including an individually attributable demonstration and a changed context or follow-up explanation; both meet the grade target. A single lesson's level 3 is that occasion's evidence, not end-of-grade mastery. Record NE/not yet assessed when evidence is missing and schedule the next check.

Device objective: [Record actual program execution/robot action if required. Paper algorithm evidence does not establish programming mastery.] Faith objective if assessed: [Reasoned choice/understanding of taught content, not strength of belief, prayer frequency or family practice.] Official alignment: [Verified URL/version/benchmark or VERIFICATION REQUIRED.]

Support: [Oral/visual directions, pre-cut/larger materials, bilingual/gesture, seated or quiet option, scribe; nonreaders do not read independently.] Challenge: [Evidence, repeat trials or new constraints, not simply extra work.] Use assessment and rubric templates for ¾-level objective-linked criteria. docs.title: Family communication and reflection
docs.text:
Send one unit newsletter at launch and completion; send an additional update if safety, schedule or objective changes. All required work occurs in school. Activities at home are optional, no-purchase and ungraded. Record actual outcomes, supply consumption, source questions, individual reteaching and changes needed before reuse.

Traceability: Local Standards -> Standards Mapping -> each linked lesson -> individual evidence. Official alignment requires verification.

docs.title: Family newsletter template
docs.text: Copy the block below once per unit; update at completion and when plans change. The family communication system includes K-6 examples. Report what actually happened, not an unconfirmed device plan.

docs.title: This week/unit in C-STREAM
docs.text:
Grade/unit/date: [ ] What we explored: [Concept in plain language.] What students did: [Build/test/measure/observe/compose/program; specify unplugged if no program ran.] What they learned: [Objective and what showed understanding.] Our Catholic connection: [A dignity, stewardship, truth or service decision; faith/source wording checked; no "God is an engineer" comparison.] Ask your child: "[Specific oral question about an actual result or choice.]" Try this at home, optional: [1-3 minutes, no purchase, account, device, outdoor exposure, photo or submission required; safe seated alternative.] Coming next/contact: [Confirmed topic; actual school-approved contact.]

No routine homework. Supplies, classroom assessment and participation do not depend on donations or completing the optional activity. Translate/read aloud using the school's actual communication arrangements; do not invent a platform. Do not publish student names, scores, photos or identifiable work without following the school's verified consent/privacy process.

Teacher-only trace: [Objective/local code; lesson; individual prompt; primary faith source/status.] Use Local Standards; official alignment requires verification. Delete teacher fields from family copy.

docs.title: C-STREAM lesson plan template
docs.text:
Version 3.0 - October 2026. Copy and complete this format; bracketed fields are author prompts, not finished instructions. Preserve a useful existing lesson, its URL and learning purpose when bringing it into this format.

C = Catholic identity; S = science; T = technology (tools and computing); R = religion/faith integration; E = engineering; A = arts, including visual art, design and music; M = mathematics, not music. Catholic identity informs purpose, dignity, truth and stewardship throughout. R names the explicit faith teaching/reflection. Art must involve an artistic decision, observation, composition or communication, not simply decorating a STEM product. Emphasize only domains students actually practice; do not claim all seven in every lesson.

docs.text: Field Complete before teaching Grade; rotation; schedule; unit; title [K/½/¾/⅚; A/B; weekly/bi-weekly; unit; title] Time [K 25 / grades 1-2 30 / grades 3-4 40 / grades 5-6 45 minutes] Big idea; why learn this? [Concept and everyday/service/vocation application] Learning objective O1 "I can [observable action + concept + success condition]." Optional O2 [Second objective only if teachable and assessable in this period] C-STREAM areas addressed [C/S/T/R/E/A/M and actual student action for each claimed domain] Catholic connection [A concrete design/ethical/stewardship decision; not prayer alone] Faith source/status [Primary-source URL, section, paraphrase/quotation status; VERIFICATION REQUIRED if unresolved] Local standards [Select from the 18-code catalog in the standards mapping section below] Official alignment [Verified source/benchmark/version, or VERIFICATION REQUIRED; never infer from a title] Technology Requirement [None / Optional / Recommended / Required; justification] Difficulty; prerequisites [Introductory/developing/complex; prior skills to check] Teacher prep [Exact minutes; Minimal <5, Light 5-15, Moderate >15-30, Significant >30] Cleanup [Minutes INCLUDED in the class period] Kit/location; readiness [Kit ID; actual location filled by school; tested by/date; unresolved blockers]

docs.text:
Word (teach 2-4) Plain-language definition Object/picture/gesture [ ] [ ] [K-1 must not depend on reading]

If a student asks "[actual likely question]": [Short answer; admit uncertainty and record a source question rather than inventing theology or science.]

Faith distinction: [Catholic belief/ethical reflection vs scientific evidence. Prayer or a saint's story is not experimental proof.]

docs.text:
• [Specific hazards, age restrictions, teacher-only steps and stop signal.]
  • [Screen allergies/sensory needs; no eating experimental materials.]
  • Never use button cells, latex balloons or projectile activities in this core program. No neodymium magnets in K; use large encapsulated ferrite magnets only where age-appropriate. Keep all small parts inaccessible to children who mouth objects. Use protected AA circuit packs; no mains power or exposed hot components.

docs.title: Exact lesson sequence
docs.text:
The following allocations total the native period and protect test/redesign, individual evidence and cleanup. Choose ONE column; replace actions with exact directions and materials. Do not add untimed prayer, transitions or worksheets.

Step K: 25 1-2: 30 3-4: 40 5-6: 45 Teacher says/does; student action 1. Hook, purpose, Catholic connection 0-3 0-3 0-4 0-4 "[Actual question]"; [brief prayer if appropriate] 2. Vocabulary, model and safety 3-7 3-8 4-10 4-11 [Demonstrate one complete action; ask a check question] 3. Plan and build/investigate 7-14 8-18 10-24 11-27 [Numbered, concrete directions; rotate builder/tester/reporter] 4. Test, compare and improve 14-19 18-23 24-32 27-36 [Same test conditions; one evidence-based change and retest] 5. Individual objective-linked check 19-22 23-27 32-37 36-41 [Each child shows/tells/draws O1; record evidence] 6. Cleanup and close 22-25 27-30 37-40 41-45 [Count, sort, disconnect, dry and return; closing thought]

Questions to ask: "[What changed?]"; "[What stayed the same?]"; "[What evidence supports your choice?]"; "[Who does this design include?]"; "[How did you avoid waste?]" Supply topic-specific versions, not just "facilitate discussion."

K-1/nonreader directions: [Show the real object, say ONE step, let students do it, repeat. Use pointing, sorting, building, gesture and dictated evidence.]

docs.title: What success looks like / individual assessment
docs.text:
Objective Individual prompt/task Meets expectation Evidence/mode Local code O1 [Actual exit question/demo] [Observable threshold] [Teacher roster: each child's response, not team product alone] [ ] O2 if taught [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ]

Use assessment and rubric formats. Levels: 1 Beginning, 2 Developing, 3 Meets Expectation, 4 Extends Learning; NE = not yet evidenced, not a zero. Participation, handwriting, neatness, confidence and artistic talent are not proxies for O1. Score an arts criterion only when that arts skill is an explicit objective.

At 25 students, gather a quick simultaneous point/show/draw response and use a planned roster sweep during hands-on time. If oral conferences need more time, record NE and schedule a check next meeting; never claim all were assessed. At expected-mastery checkpoints, Local Standards requires two dated observations on separate occasions with an individual demonstration and changed context/follow-up explanation. One exit check alone does not establish end-of-grade mastery.

docs.title: Support and challenge
docs.text:
Support: [Read aloud; fewer choices; pre-cut pieces; larger tools; bilingual vocabulary/gesture; seated/quiet option; adult scribing. Keep the same concept unless explicitly documenting an objective change.]

Challenge: [Add a justified constraint, repeat trial, compare data, or explain a tradeoff. Do not routinely turn faster learners into helpers.]

docs.title: If things go wrong
docs.text: Problem Exact response Objective preserved or changed? Structure/test fails [Stabilize supports; change one variable; record failure as evidence] [ ] Supplies missing [Named safe substitution, quantity and changed constraint] [ ] Devices/network/loan unavailable [Unplugged task or reschedule] Programming/robot operation needs later real-device evidence Early finishers [Specific extension] [ ] Time short Stop new building; keep individual check and cleanup; continue later [Unfinished evidence recorded] Unsafe condition Stop affected activity; safe seated fallback; notify responsible adult [Do not silently continue]

docs.text:
1. [Stop tests; switch off/disconnect packs; teacher counts hazardous parts.]
  2. [Sort reusable vs waste; dry all wet materials; wipe tables per school practice.]
  3. [Restock exact quantities; label broken kit OUT OF SERVICE and report.]
  4. [Record elapsed time, individual evidence, supply use and next reteach.]

Copy the newsletter block. Include what children did/learned, a Catholic connection, a specific oral question, and an optional no-purchase activity. No routine homework.

docs.title: Standards mapping
docs.text: Use only the local catalog: CST-C1/C2/C3, CST-S1/S2/S3, CST-T1/T2/T3, CST-E1/E2/E3, CST-A1/A2/A3, CST-M1/M2/M3. Definitions and grade expectations belong to Local Standards, not this template. Use Standards Mapping for the chain standard -> grade -> unit -> lesson -> objective -> individual evidence.

docs.text:
• Native timings sum correctly, including cleanup.
  • Complete kit and scaling confirmed for actual enrollment.
  • Teacher background, model, safety, misconceptions and failure responses supplied.
  • Each assessed objective has an individual prompt and success condition.
  • Support, challenge, indoor and no-device contingencies are explicit.
  • Faith/source claims accurate or marked VERIFICATION REQUIRED.
  • Family copy prepared; no home purchase, donation or device prerequisite.
  • Substitute has named contact and actual materials location.

docs.text: Use the unit template as the planning record and lesson template for each meeting. This project overlay preserves Launch -> Research -> Create -> Present without creating a competing lesson format. Version 3.0 - October 2026.

docs.text:
Success criteria: [Measurable conditions, not "beautiful," "creative" or "participates well."] Constraints: [Time, materials, safety, cost.] Team roles/rotation: [Builder/tester/reporter; each child gets a hands-on turn.] Individual deliverable: [Show/tell/draw/record; use the student sheet or nonreader card rather than a mandatory written report.] Arts objective if used: [Composition, pattern, observation, musical phrase or visual communication; assess the named skill rather than expensive presentation.]

Complete the unit's materials/safety/support/challenge/fallback sections, including 10/15/20/25 scaling, teacher-only prep, exact test and cleanup. Retain records between meetings in labeled bins; no fragile work transported home as a requirement. School supplies and work time cover participation.

docs.text:
• Who might benefit? [An authentic, respectfully described user need.]
  • Which decision honors dignity or care for creation? [Actual example.]
  • Faith source: [Primary URL/section; VERIFICATION REQUIRED if unverified.]
  • Classroom model vs actual service: [Do not claim a prototype has helped people without evidence. Do not deploy assistive/medical/structural devices or drinking-water filters without qualified adult review.]

docs.title: Assessment and family copy
docs.text:
Use the assessment template and student project rubric. Share 1-3 objective-linked criteria before launch. No universal 100-point or faith/ presentation weighting. Technical evidence and faith reasoning remain distinguishable; neither team success nor enthusiasm proves individual mastery.

Use the newsletter template at launch and completion. No routine homework, home research, donation, purchased board, family attendance or personal device required. Optional no-purchase family conversation: "[One actual question a child can answer orally.]"

docs.title: Before reuse
docs.text: Record observed prep/cleanup minutes, consumables per cohort, individual evidence still missing, unsafe/missing parts, verified sources, objective changes and revisions. Use Standards Mapping to connect only practiced standards from Local Standards.

docs.title: Objective-linked rubric template
docs.text:
Grade/unit/lesson: [ ] Objective/code: [ ] Prompt: [ ] Modes/support: [Show/tell/draw/record, read-aloud/scribe/larger materials.] Select 1-3 criteria genuinely taught. State the Meets condition first.

Criterion linked to objective 1 Beginning 2 Developing 3 Meets Expectation 4 Extends Learning (optional) [Observable concept/action] [Evidence reveals named misconception or missing action] [Partial evidence; specify missing part] [Exact success condition] [Transfers/explains using additional evidence; not beyond-grade content by default]

For a three-level rubric omit column 4; do not relabel NE as Beginning. NE: not yet evidenced sits outside the scale.

docs.title: Completed example
docs.text:
O1: Compare flat and folded paper using an equal span and load.

Criterion 1 Beginning 2 Developing 3 Meets Expectation 4 Extends Learning Evidence-based comparison Names a result different from the observed test Names the observed stronger design but cannot identify the common test condition yet Names the observed result and shows equal span and load placement Repeats the fair test and explains whether the second result supports the first

A collapsed bridge can still meet this objective. Decorative skill, participation, handwriting, family help and confident speech are not this criterion. If the objective is a rhythmic pattern or visual composition, write a separate arts criterion measuring that named artistic decision, not "looks beautiful." Assess Catholic reasoning from taught content, not a child's interior faith.

Scoring/evidence record: use Assessment Template. One Meets rating is evidence for that occasion. Expected-mastery checkpoints require two dated observations on separate occasions under Local Standards, not one polished project. Source/status: local teacher criterion; official standards alignment requires verification in Standards Mapping.

docs.title: Standards mapping template
docs.text:
The definitions belong to Local Standards. The 18 local codes are CST-C1/C2/C3, CST-S1/S2/S3, CST-T1/T2/T3, CST-E1/E2/E3, CST-A1/A2/A3 and CST-M1/M2/M3. R faith integration is recorded with the Catholic domain; music belongs to A. Do not invent CST-R or music-as-M codes.

docs.text:
Authority/framework Version/applicable year Exact benchmark/code/text or paraphrase Primary URL/document/section Lesson evidence Verified by/date/status [Minnesota / Archdiocese / CSTA / other] [ ] [Do not invent] [ ] [ ] [VERIFICATION REQUIRED until checked]

Local codes are not official Archdiocesan or state standards. Consult the shared review's source record; source or Church quotation questions remain VERIFICATION REQUIRED until checked against the primary document.

Music is a genuine part of A in C-STREAM, but the local catalog chiefly defines visual observation/design/communication and does not certify full music standards coverage. Map a music task only where its action actually meets a catalog competency; verify any official music benchmark separately. Do not create a music-as-M code or invent an extra local domain.
